correctness.rationale: Expand the fourth moment exactly by parity; repetitions yield 3S²-2 sum a_e⁴ and every four-cycle yields 24 product. Pairwise disjointness makes the displayed exact nonnegative defect decomposition valid. AM--GM makes each local deficit nonnegative, forcing one-square support and signed coefficient equality; in the no-square case Cauchy--Schwarz yields 3-2/m. The mass inequalities t >=1-delta >1/2 and 1-delta <= t²+(1-t)² yield the precise threshold, attained by two disjoint uniform squares. Exact-rational program checks 24 finite examples only; the infinite graph-family result is proved analytically.

originality.rationale: The full primary comparisons show general 2-to-4 norm complexity, Rademacher moment comparisons, and unweighted graph-quadric 4-cycle count asymptotics, not a universal sharp real coefficient norm and optimal four-cycle mass-concentration law for graphs with pairwise edge-disjoint squares. Prior same-domain cube-graph results concern a fixed graph whose square faces overlap in edges, and do not imply the structural classification. The graph fourth-moment expansion is historical technology; only the exact class-wide sharp theorem with rigidity and stability is proposed as original, with an acknowledged residual historical-equivalence risk.
residual_risks: A classical additive-energy or Sidon set packing inequality not indexed by searches might yield the same class-wide bound or its sharp stability function.

The method is elementary after the moment identity; the distinctive proposed contributions are the full real graph-class classification, equality rigidity, and sharp dimension-free localization, not that identity itself.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies an intrinsic norm of a natural and size-unbounded class of graph-supported Walsh subspaces, exhibits a fourth-moment isometry for all square-free graphs, rigidly characterizes all extremizers in the square-bearing class, and proves the dimension-free optimal concentration of every sufficiently near-maximizer on a four-cycle. This sharp functional-analytic stability result addresses meaningful near-extremizer structure, not merely a small numerical bound or arbitrary graph-instance table.
